summary:
MARS REMNANTS is an interactive educational platform that explores the human-made equipment left behind on the surface of Mars during NASA's robotic exploration missions. While rovers and landers receive significant attention, the engineering components discarded during landing and deployment also tell important stories about space exploration.

Our project brings these forgotten artifacts into focus through interactive equipment exploration, mission-based storytelling, engineering explanations, historical timelines and NASA reference materials. Users can discover components such as Perseverance's parachute, backshell, heat shield and sky-crane descent stage, understanding their original purposes and roles in successful Mars landings.

Designed for students, researchers and space enthusiasts, MARS REMNANTS transforms mission information into an engaging learning experience, helping preserve the engineering history of Mars exploration and inspiring curiosity about future space missions.
details: MARS REMNANTS – Interactive Mars Hardware Explorer Team: GETTAFIE 2.0 Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars. 1. Problem Statement Mars exploration missions are remembered mainly for their rovers and scientific discoveries. However, reaching the Martian surface requires complex engineering systems, many of which separate from the spacecraft and remain on the planet after completing their purpose. Components such as parachutes, backshells, heat shields and powered descent stages represent important engineering achievements, yet their stories often receive less attention. 2. Our Proposed Solution MARS REMNANTS is an interactive educational platform designed to explore the engineering, scientific and historical stories behind NASA hardware left on Mars. Using NASA mission documentation and orbital imagery, our platform transforms information about Mars landing equipment into an engaging digital exploration experience. Our initial case study focuses on NASA's Mars 2020 Perseverance landing system at Jezero Crater. 3. Main Features Interactive Hardware Explorer: Users can explore different landing components, including the parachute, backshell, heat shield and powered descent stage, through interactive information cards. Mission Storytelling: An interactive timeline explains the major stages of the Perseverance landing, from atmospheric entry to successful touchdown. Mars Landing-Site Exploration: NASA orbital imagery helps users understand the documented locations and distribution of landing-system components around the landing site. Engineering Learning: Educational explanations introduce thermal protection, aerodynamic drag, parachute deceleration and the sky-crane landing mechanism. Knowledge Check: An interactive quiz allows visitors to test their understanding of Mars landing technology. NASA References: Each major engineering explanation is supported by links to relevant NASA mission resources. 4. Technical Implementation The website is developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. - HTML provides the website structure. - CSS provides responsive layouts, visual design and animations. - JavaScript powers interactive hardware cards, filters, mission timelines and educational activities. - NASA imagery and mission documentation provide the scientific foundation. The website is designed as a lightweight, responsive experience accessible through desktop and mobile browsers. It is hosted using GitHub Pages. 5. Creativity and Innovation Rather than focusing exclusively on the rover, MARS REMNANTS explores the forgotten engineering systems that made successful Mars landings possible. The project presents these components as an interactive engineering archive, connecting their original functions with their roles in the history of planetary exploration. 6. Scientific Relevance and Validity The project uses NASA's documented Mars 2020 landing-site imagery and NASA/JPL engineering information. The distinction between operational spacecraft and discarded landing equipment is maintained. Perseverance itself is presented as the mission's scientific rover, not as abandoned equipment. The project avoids inventing artifact coordinates or unsupported scientific claims. 7. Target Audience and Expected Impact The platform is designed for students, educators, researchers and space enthusiasts. It aims to: - Improve understanding of planetary landing engineering. - Make NASA mission information more accessible. - Encourage curiosity about space exploration. - Highlight the engineering history preserved on the Martian surface. 8. Future Development Future improvements may include additional Mars missions, verified geospatial artifact mapping, 3D Mars surface exploration, more interactive engineering models and multilingual educational resources. Conclusion MARS REMNANTS gives attention to the machines that completed their mission but remained behind. By connecting engineering, scientific evidence and storytelling, our project makes the forgotten hardware of Mars exploration part of the story of human discovery. Project: MARS REMNANTS Team: GETTAFIE 2.0 NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
